questions.question: What is the main warning given at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Not every reader will understand all of the book, but each reader can still gain some benefit from it.

questions.question: What example is used to show that different readers can benefit in different amounts?
questions.answer: A garden is used as the example, where each person can reach only some of the fruit.

questions.question: What does the garden example teach about learning from the book?
questions.answer: It teaches that a person does not need to understand everything to receive something valuable.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for why the book is hard to understand?
questions.answer: Five reasons are given.

questions.question: What is the first reason for the difficulty?
questions.answer: The book was written from the writer’s own understanding and for his own use, not shaped around what other people usually understand.

questions.question: How does the second reason make the subjects harder?
questions.answer: The topics are very wide, deep, and sometimes long, so many people cannot take them in all at once.

questions.question: What is special about the teaching described in the second reason?
questions.answer: It explains belief in Allah’s oneness in a very complete and far-reaching way.

questions.question: According to the third reason, why can one sentence become very long?
questions.answer: It can become long so the full truth is not broken apart and so needed background can be included.

questions.question: What does the third reason show about giving proof?
questions.answer: It shows that one proof may need many steps and explanations before it is complete.

questions.question: According to the fourth reason, why might the discussion feel too long to some readers?
questions.answer: It includes many different proofs and signs for the same point, which can make the explanation lengthy.

questions.question: What does the fourth reason suggest about some readers?
questions.answer: Some readers may struggle because their understanding is not strong enough to follow many proofs.

questions.question: What does the fifth reason say about the time when the book was written?
questions.answer: It was written quickly during Ramadan while the writer was upset and physically sick.

questions.question: Why was the first draft not revised in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The writer felt he was not writing by his own choice, so he thought it was not fitting to change it by his own ideas later.

questions.question: Besides haste and illness, what other thing in the fifth reason made the book harder for some readers?
questions.answer: Some parts were in Arabic, and one whole section in Arabic was taken out and made into a separate work.

questions.question: What comfort is given to readers who cannot understand everything in the book?
questions.answer: They are told that they will still receive a share of benefit.

questions.question: Why is the book compared to a garden with fruit?
questions.answer: Because a garden has more than one person can reach, just as the book has more than one reader can fully grasp.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the purpose of the garden?
questions.answer: It is not made for just one person, but for many people with different abilities.

questions.question: What can we infer about the readers from the garden picture?
questions.answer: Readers have different levels of understanding, and that is normal.

questions.question: What is the first cause of difficulty based on?
questions.answer: It is based on the writer recording what he himself saw and understood.

questions.question: How is this book said to be different from many other books?
questions.answer: It was not written to match the common ideas and understanding of other people.

questions.question: Why does the second cause say the topics are hard to grasp quickly?
questions.answer: Because they deal with a very broad and deep explanation of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: In the third cause, why is it important not to split up a truth too much?
questions.answer: Because breaking it apart too much could weaken or damage the full meaning.

questions.question: What does the third cause teach about deep subjects?
questions.answer: Deep subjects may need long explanations even if they begin from a single sentence.

questions.question: What is the problem mentioned in the fourth cause?
questions.answer: Many proofs are given for one matter, and that can feel overwhelming to some readers.

questions.question: Why might someone with limited understanding find the fourth cause difficult?
questions.answer: Because following many proofs in one discussion can be hard to keep up with.

questions.question: What spiritual detail is mentioned in the fifth cause about how the book came?
questions.answer: Its insights are said to have come during Ramadan.

questions.question: What personal hardships are mentioned in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The writer was troubled, sick, and wrote in a rushed way.

questions.question: How did the Arabic material affect the book’s ease of understanding?
questions.answer: It made the book harder for some readers, especially since one fully Arabic section was separated out.

questions.question: What promise does the passage make to every reader, even if understanding is incomplete?
questions.answer: Every reader will still receive some benefit.

questions.question: What does the image of fruit within reach represent?
questions.answer: It represents the part of the book a person is able to understand.

questions.question: What do the “longer arms” in the example stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for people who can understand more.

questions.question: Why is it important that the passage says the book is not only for one kind of reader?
questions.answer: It shows that readers can differ and still each have a place in benefiting from it.

questions.question: What is the first listed reason the book may be hard for others?
questions.answer: The writer followed his own understanding instead of shaping the work around other people’s ways of thinking.

questions.question: How could writing mainly for oneself make a book harder for others?
questions.answer: Some explanations may fit the writer’s own mind better than the readers’ minds.

questions.question: What topic in the second reason makes the work especially weighty?
questions.answer: A very full explanation of the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What three qualities of the subjects are named in the second reason?
questions.answer: They are wide, deep, and sometimes long.

questions.question: Why might one sentence cover a whole page according to the third reason?
questions.answer: Because a large truth may need a long explanation to stay complete.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying one proof needs many beginnings or preparations?
questions.answer: It means readers may need background steps before they can understand the proof itself.

questions.question: In the fourth reason, about how many proofs might be used for one point?
questions.answer: Sometimes ten or twenty proofs might be used.

questions.question: What effect can using so many proofs have on the writing?
questions.answer: It can make the writing seem wordy and difficult.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, what was the writer’s physical condition while writing?
questions.answer: He was suffering from several illnesses.

questions.question: What was the writer’s attitude toward changing what he had written?
questions.answer: He felt it would not be right to rearrange or fix it based on his own later thoughts.

questions.question: Name two things in the fifth reason that added to the book’s difficulty.
questions.answer: It was written quickly without revision, and some sections were in Arabic.

questions.question: What big idea is given before the five reasons are listed?
questions.answer: Even if the whole book is not understood, no sincere reader leaves empty-handed.

questions.question: What can a reader learn about fairness from the garden example?
questions.answer: One book can serve people with different abilities, not just one kind of person.

questions.question: How many causes of difficulty are named in the passage?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: In the first cause, whose understanding guided the writing?
questions.answer: The writer’s own understanding guided it.

questions.question: Why might that first cause create a challenge for readers?
questions.answer: Readers may not think in the same way the writer does.

questions.question: In the second cause, what makes the subject matter especially hard?
questions.answer: It presents a complete and far-reaching discussion of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What does the second cause tell us about the size of the ideas in the book?
questions.answer: The ideas are very large and deep, so they are not easy to take in quickly.

questions.question: According to the third cause, why is a short style not always possible?
questions.answer: Because shortening too much might damage a large truth or leave out needed groundwork.

questions.question: What is included in the fourth cause besides basic statements?
questions.answer: Many evidences and demonstrations are included.

questions.question: What result can come from adding many evidences?
questions.answer: The explanation can become lengthy and hard for some minds to follow.

questions.question: What time of year is connected with the inspiration of the treatise in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: Ramadan is connected with it.

questions.question: What emotional and physical struggles are mentioned in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The writer was troubled inwardly and also suffering in his body.

questions.question: What happened to the fully Arabic first section mentioned in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: It was removed from this book and turned into a separate work.

questions.question: What should a reader expect if the book feels difficult?
questions.answer: The reader should still expect to benefit from it in some way.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens when a person enters the “garden”?
questions.answer: The person can reach some of the good things there, even if not all of them.

questions.question: What lesson about ability is taught by the image of different arm lengths?
questions.answer: People have different levels of ability, and that changes how much they can take in.

questions.question: How is the structure of the passage organized after the opening example?
questions.answer: It lists five separate reasons for the book’s difficulty.

questions.question: What is the heart of the first reason?
questions.answer: The book came from the writer’s own personal understanding and was not adjusted for everyone else.

questions.question: Why does that first reason matter for comprehension?
questions.answer: Because writing for oneself can make the path of thought harder for others to follow.

questions.question: What belief-centered topic is named in the second reason?
questions.answer: The topic is the oneness of Allah explained in a very complete way.

questions.question: Why does the second reason say some people cannot understand everything right away?
questions.answer: Because the matters are very broad, deep, and sometimes long.

questions.question: What does the third reason say about the size of a single truth?
questions.answer: A single truth can be so large that it needs a very long explanation.

questions.question: Why might one proof not fit into a short sentence?
questions.answer: Because it may need many earlier explanations before the proof becomes clear.

questions.question: What is one effect of having many proofs in the fourth reason?
questions.answer: It can make the discussion feel stretched out.

questions.question: What kind of reader is especially challenged by the fourth reason?
questions.answer: A reader with weaker understanding may find it hard.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, what shows that the writing process was not calm and polished?
questions.answer: The book was written quickly during hardship and the first draft was left without revision.

questions.question: Why did the writer avoid correcting the draft afterward?
questions.answer: He believed the writing did not come simply from his own personal choice, so changing it by his own thoughts seemed wrong.

questions.question: What language issue in the fifth reason could make reading harder for some people?
questions.answer: Some parts were in Arabic, including a section that was later separated.

questions.question: What encouraging message is given to someone who cannot fully understand the treatise?
questions.answer: That person can still receive a helpful portion from it.

questions.question: What object is used to compare the treatise to something rich and full?
questions.answer: It is compared to a garden full of fruit.

questions.question: In that comparison, what does being able to reach only some fruit mean?
questions.answer: It means understanding only part of the book.

questions.question: What does the comparison teach about readers who understand more than others?
questions.answer: It teaches that some are able to take more, but the book still benefits everyone.

questions.question: What is the first cause that makes the book difficult?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own view and not according to the way other people usually understand things.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the style of such a book?
questions.answer: Its style may be personal and not always easy for every reader to follow.

questions.question: What makes the second cause especially serious in content?
questions.answer: It deals with a very complete explanation of belief in Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Which words in the passage describe the subjects in the second cause?
questions.answer: They are described as very broad, very deep, and sometimes very long.

questions.question: According to the third cause, why might a sentence continue for a whole page?
questions.answer: Because the writer wants to keep a big truth whole and include what is needed to explain it.

questions.question: What does the third cause say about the relationship between proof and preparation?
questions.answer: It says a proof may require a lot of preparation first.

questions.question: What does the fourth cause add to the picture of difficulty?
questions.answer: It explains that many proofs may be gathered for one matter, making the discussion long.

questions.question: Why do many proofs not always make a text easier for everyone?
questions.answer: Because too many steps and examples can be hard for some readers to process.

questions.question: What conditions surrounded the writing of the book in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The writer was in Ramadan, distressed, ill, and writing quickly.

questions.question: How did the writer view his role while writing?
questions.answer: He felt he was not simply acting by his own will.

questions.question: What final details in the fifth cause show why some readers might struggle even more?
questions.answer: Some passages were in Arabic, and the first section in Arabic was removed into another work.
